newsitem.title: HUNGARY: RICHTER Q1 SALES UP TO ALL MARKETS.
newsitem.headline: RICHTER Q1 SALES UP TO ALL MARKETS.

text.p: Hungarian pharmaceuticals company Richter Gedeon Rt's sales of finished products rose in all of its markets in the first quarter of 1997, the company said in its earnings report on Tuesday.

"Increases in sales of finished products were achieved in each of the company's four main geographical regions - Hungary, CIS, Eastern Europe and the rest of the world," Richter said in its earnings report which was published in the official gazette of the Budapest Stock Exchange.
Richter's total sales in January-March 1997 rose to 12.801 billion forints from 9.419 billion in the same period of 1996, while its net profit rose to 4.997 billion from 3.258 billion.

Main contributors to a rise in domestic sales to 4.529 billion forints from 3.38 billion in the same period of 1996 were antihypertensive Ednyt, antiulcer Quamatel and the OTC multivitamin products Centrum and the sore throat medicine Strepsils, it said.
"During the quarter Ednyt became the company's leading product in Hungary measured by sales value, overtaking Cavinton," it said.
Richter's sales to the CIS countries surged to 3.905 billion forints from 2.284 billion, with sales benefiting to some extent from an average price increase of four percent effective January 1, 1997.
Richter said good sales growth was reported from most CIS countries, notably Russia and the Ukraine which represent the largest markets for the company's products in the CIS.
Eastern European sales expanded to 1.558 billion forints in January-March 1997 from 1.051 billion in the same three months of 1996, with Poland remaining the largest market for Richter in the region.
"Progress was impeded in the Czech Republic where budget problems leading to slow payments have resulted in sales to hospitals being restricted," the report said.
On other markets Richter's sales rose to 2.809 billion forints from 2.704 billion, with sales of bulk and other products declining, but of finished products rising.
